spans.complaint_escalation: No true resolution for complaint submission as I was complaining about my unresolved buyback request

notes: Repeated reconsideration submissions, a prior complaint closed without a fix, then a call to a live rep -- 2.3 explicit-count/prior-complaint-closed. Administrative forbearance here is a servicer status blocking PSLF counts, not a hardship request, so no 2.2 mark.

Borderline escalation: he did file a complaint on the company site before this filing, but it is a single prior complaint with no stated outcome, and it was to the tow yard rather than the loan firm. 2.3 exclusion (one contact) plus 3.4. Repossession is named in 2.2's mark list, but he calls it 'wrongfully repossessed' and states no money shortage anywhere -- 2.2 exclusion (charge/action being wrong, not affordability) plus 3.4.

Overdraft fees, but the customer's own case is that funds were sufficient -- 2.2 exclusion, a charge being wrong is not distress. No prior contact with the firm; the only escalation is this filing (2.3).
Same reasoning as 11614709: fee-dispute framing asserts sufficient funds (2.2 exclusion); escalation is the CFPB filing only (2.3).

A charge-off implies past non-payment but no shortage of money is described and the framing is a credit-reporting/tax-form dispute -- 2.2 exclusion plus 3.4. 'I have requested' is a single ask (2.3 exclusion).

spans.financial_distress: Due to having low income the payment plan did not apply to my forbearance with navient.

notes: 2.2 mark list: income shortage plus a forbearance (hardship-programme) request.

spans.complaint_escalation: The bank provided a resolution letter that is to the XXXXXXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX which was supposed to be for them and then later this week another response from this bank which confused me about whether response is accuracy.

notes: Two bank resolution letters and a case number about the same question, still unanswered -- 2.3 prior reference/case number and prior complaint closed without a fix. The closure was the bank's decision ('a business 's decision to end your deposit relationship'), so 2.1's de-banking exclusion applies and churn is false.

spans.complaint_escalation: I have told them numerous times to fix the fraud and if they don't, which they never have, I have forewarned them that I can and will file a complaint against their financial institution for fraud.

notes: Repeat calls to the firm about the same unresolved fee problem (2.3). Threatening to complain further is explicitly not churn (2.1). Funds are present but access-blocked, and the substance is a fee dispute -- 2.2 exclusion.

Textbook 2.3 exclusion: 'reached out to customer service ... not provided with a satisfactory response' is one contact and dissatisfaction with the answer. Firm cancelled the account, so 2.1 de-banking exclusion.
Request to close accounts the customer never opened -- 2.1 fraud/identity-theft exclusion. The prior filing was to the FTC, another regulator, not to the firm (2.3).

spans.churn_intent: I am closing both of the accounts I have with them immediately, but will pay off my balances.

notes: Customer-initiated closure with dissatisfaction (2.1 mark). 'Very high minimum payments' is a billing-accuracy dispute and he states he will pay the balances -- 2.2 exclusion.

spans.complaint_escalation: Despite my efforts to contact customer service multiple times, I was not provided with a reason for the closures.

notes: Explicit repeat contact, same problem, unresolved (2.3). Firm-initiated closure -- 2.1 de-banking exclusion. 'Significant financial impact' is lost points/$50 cashback, not an ability-to-pay problem (2.2).

spans.financial_distress: the balance goes up to the point that I will be not able to pay off

notes: Genuinely borderline. The complaint's spine is an undisclosed annual fee, which is the 2.2 exclusion (a charge being wrong). But he additionally states a prospective inability to pay off the balance, and 2.2's mark list includes 'fear of default'. Marked on that clause. 'I am a XXXX senior citizen' is a status, not a stated change, and the XXXX is not guessed at -- 3.3 -- so no life_event.

spans.churn_intent: I closed the account because I was misled to believe I could stabilize my balance without accruing interest.

notes: Customer-initiated closure, and not the purely-administrative kind 2.1 excludes -- there is dissatisfaction and a stated reason. 'Stabilize my balance' hints at balance pressure but he reports 100% on-time payments and no shortage, so 3.4 says do not mark distress.
Single call escalated to a supervisor within that same call -- 2.3 exclusion (contacted once, dissatisfied). The declined purchase is not attributed to lack of funds (2.2).

spans.churn_intent: She offered promotions to keep my account open but I decided to close it.
spans.complaint_escalation: I call and speak to Amex and at their request work to get charges credited through the vendor. While this is ongoing I repeatedly get charged late fees and interest.

notes: Churn is unambiguous: retention offer refused, customer closed. Escalation is the hard call -- no explicit count or case number, but there is a call, an ongoing firm-directed remediation process, and a later offer to settle, all on the same unresolved problem, which is 2.3's headline (raised before, still unresolved) rather than its one-contact exclusion. Distress is false: the 90-days-past-due status comes from deliberate withholding of fees/interest in protest, which is the 2.2 exclusion.

spans.complaint_escalation: I have previously disputed the negative reporting of late payments by XXXX and XXXX on my credit report.

notes: Explicit prior dispute to the same firm/bureaus, unresolved (2.3). The late payments are disputed as inaccurate, not described as unaffordable, and 'limit my ability to qualify for essential financing' is credit access, not an obligation he cannot meet (2.2).

spans.complaint_escalation: My last attempt was at beginning of this year and my denial email was received on XX/XX/year>.
spans.life_event: I am an XXXX servicemember and requested that American Express ( AMEX ) apply SCRA benefits to my account ( s ) in accordance with 50 U.S.C. 39014043.

notes: Two borderline calls in one document. life_event: 2.4 lists military deployment; active-duty service with enlistment orders is the closest thing in this set to that, though it is arguably a status rather than a change -- flagged for adjudication. complaint_escalation: 'My last attempt' implies a series of prior attempts, plus a documented request-and-denial cycle; weaker than 2.3's explicit-count example. An interest-rate reduction claimed as a statutory right is not distress (2.2).

spans.churn_intent: I have since transferred by paycheck and XXXX XXXX check to XXXX XXXX Bank.
spans.complaint_escalation: I went into the XXXX  branch and I was told they were locked out too and nothing can be done.

notes: Churn is the 2.1 direct-deposit example almost verbatim -- he moved his paycheck to another bank and wants out. Note the inversion: the account is frozen by the firm (which alone would be the de-banking exclusion), but the customer's own stated intent to leave and completed move of deposits is what earns the mark. Escalation: a written request, a phone call, and a branch visit, all unresolved (2.3). Distress is false -- he cannot reach his money because of a firm freeze, not because of a shortage, and no unmet obligation is stated (3.4).

spans.complaint_escalation: The only way I discovered my fraud case had been closed was by calling Navy Federal multiple times.

notes: Multiple appeals, multiple calls, case closed with no written response (2.3). $14,000 was drained by a fraudster, but no inability to meet an obligation follows from it and the 'distress' described is emotional -- 3.4 says do not mark 2.2.

spans.complaint_escalation: I have submitted three appeal letters with no response.

notes: Explicit count of prior appeals to the firm, unanswered (2.3). Collection pressure is present but the dispute is over whether the debt is owed, not affordability (2.2). 'Affecting my mental health' is a consequence of the banking dispute, not a circumstance outside it, and the 'XXXX XXXX' redaction is not guessed at -- 2.4 and 3.3.
A disputed $18 charge and an app review. Leaving a public review is not contact with the firm about a repeat problem (2.3) and is not a statement about ending the relationship (2.1).

spans.complaint_escalation: after calling them 3 time till this day they answer alway is that the credit card is being delivered.

notes: 2.3's explicit-count example, same problem, still unresolved.

Bank closed both accounts with no notice -- 2.1 de-banking exclusion, the opposite of churn. Credit-score and business damage are harms, not a described inability to meet obligations (2.2). No prior contact with the firm (2.3).

spans.complaint_escalation: Goldman Sachs has denied my dispute three times without adequately addressing the facts presented.

notes: Explicit count, a dispute case number, and repeated reopen-and-deny cycles (2.3). The medication safety issue does not state an illness of the customer, so 3.4 keeps life_event unmarked.

The trap case for 2.3. There is a prior complaint, but it was to the CFPB, not to the firm, and the customer's own point is that it concerned a different bank and card -- 2.3 excludes both the regulator filing itself and multiple contacts about different problems.

spans.complaint_escalation: I also called into Capital One to speak with a customer service supervisor to explain the situation and also put in a complaint

notes: Two credit-line-increase requests plus a supervisor call in which he tried to lodge a complaint and was told none could be taken -- raised before, unresolved (2.3). Borderline in that the two requests are applications rather than complaints. Churn is explicitly negated by the customer: 'Me closing my account isnt an option.' Distress is false -- he states a high income, no rent or mortgage, and a perfect payment record; maxing a low limit is a utilisation problem, not a 2.2 shortage.

spans.complaint_escalation: I can not get anywhere and I have dealt with about XXXX different people.

notes: A year of being passed between people on the same unresolved servicing problem (2.3). Hardest distress call in the set: 'I would love to stay in my home w my family' reads like the foreclosure fear 2.2 lists, but he never says he is behind or short of money and he cites his job and police pension as capacity, so 3.4 resolves it to unmarked. The pension is stated as an income source, not as a retirement event, so no life_event (2.4, 3.4).

spans.complaint_escalation: I tried disputing this do to faulty information on my credit report and never got a response

notes: Borderline against 2.3's one-contact exclusion. Marked because that exclusion covers a customer who was answered and is dissatisfied; here no answer ever came, which is the same shape as 2.3's 'promised callback that did not come', and the problem was raised before and is still unresolved.

spans.complaint_escalation: I have contacted and spoke with many representatives from Selene Finance and XXXX XXXX XXXX to resolve this issue.

notes: Many representatives, same escrow problem, firm non-compliant (2.3). The threatened $540/month increase is contested as improper -- a charge being wrong, 2.2 exclusion -- and no inability to pay is stated.
